input.reasoning:
Estimation approach: Convert story points to engineering hours using a standard reference (1 point ≈ 6-7 hours of blended dev effort for a mid-complexity team), then split hours across roles based on task nature (backend-heavy, frontend-heavy, infra, QA, migration). Total backlog = 5+8+8+13+8+5+13+21 = 81 points.

Role allocation logic per task:
- PW-1 (CI/staging, 5pts): DevOps-led, some Backend support.
- PW-2 (Design system, 8pts): Frontend-led, light QA.
- PW-3 (Registration/login, 8pts): Backend-led, Frontend UI, QA testing, security-sensitive so Urgent priority gets more QA.
- PW-4 (RBAC, 13pts): Backend-led (API enforcement), Frontend (UI permission gating), QA.
- PW-5 (Dashboard, 8pts): Frontend-led, Backend API support, QA.
- PW-6 (Invoice list/detail, 5pts): Frontend-led, Backend API, QA.
- PW-7 (Payment integration, 13pts): Backend-led (Stripe/webhooks/reconciliation), QA heavy (payment correctness), DevOps for webhook infra.
- PW-8 (Legacy migration, 21pts): Backend-led (ETL scripts), DevOps (environment/cutover), QA (data validation) - large effort, no frontend.

Using ~7 hours/point blended baseline, adjusted per role split. I built a per-task hour breakdown summing to role totals, checking against FTE capacity over an assumed ~3-month (13-week) delivery window:
- Backend: 1.5 FTE x 13 weeks x 37.5 hrs/wk ≈ 731 hrs capacity (using ~40hr week minus overhead ~37.5). I'll allocate ~650 hrs to backend, within capacity.
- Frontend: 1.0 FTE x 13 weeks x 37.5 ≈ 487 hrs capacity. Allocate ~380 hrs.
- QA: 0.6 FTE x 13 weeks x 37.5 ≈ 292 hrs capacity. Allocate ~230 hrs.
- DevOps: 0.4 FTE x 13 weeks x 37.5 ≈ 195 hrs capacity. Allocate ~140 hrs.

Detailed per-task hours (Backend/Frontend/QA/DevOps):
PW-1: BE 10, FE 0, QA 8, DevOps 40
PW-2: BE 0, FE 70, QA 15, DevOps 0
PW-3: BE 70, FE 40, QA 25, DevOps 5
PW-4: BE 110, FE 55, QA 30, DevOps 5
PW-5: BE 55, FE 65, QA 20, DevOps 0
PW-6: BE 40, FE 45, QA 15, DevOps 0
PW-7: BE 120, FE 20, QA 50, DevOps 25
PW-8: BE 160, FE 0, QA 35, DevOps 40 (plus migration tooling)

Sum Backend: 10+0+70+110+55+40+120+160 = 565 hrs
Sum Frontend: 0+70+40+55+65+45+20+0 = 295 hrs
Sum QA: 8+15+25+30+20+15+50+35 = 198 hrs
Sum DevOps: 40+0+5+5+0+0+25+40 = 115 hrs

These fit within capacity estimates for a ~3-month timeline, with Backend and DevOps running fairly hot relative to their FTE, flagged as assumption.

Costs:
Backend: 565 x 98.33 = 55,556.45
Frontend: 295 x 90 = 26,550
QA: 198 x 70 = 13,860
DevOps: 115 x 110 = 12,650

Total labour = 55,556.45+26,550+13,860+12,650 = 108,616.45

Non-labour: environment/hosting costs for staging + migration tooling, Stripe sandbox fees, PM/contingency for data migration risk, and third-party data migration tooling licence.

Priority breakdown (sum task costs by priority) — approximate by allocating cost proportionally to points within priority groups:
Total points = 81, total labour cost = 108,616.45 → cost/point ≈ 1341.

Urgent points: PW-3(8)+PW-7(13)=21 → cost ≈ 21*1341=28,161
High points: PW-1(5)+PW-4(13)+PW-5(8)+PW-8(21)=47 → cost ≈ 47*1341=63,027
Medium points: PW-2(8)+PW-6(5)=13 → cost ≈13*1341=17,433

(rounded to sum ~108,621, close enough given rounding)

Scenarios: base case = sum of labour+non-labour; optimistic (P50) slightly lower assuming efficiencies; pessimistic (P90) higher accounting for migration/integration risk overruns, especially PW-8 and PW-7 which have high uncertainty (data migration scale, Stripe reconciliation edge cases).

No historical actuals exist, so estimate uncertainty is wider than usual; flagged as assumption.

nonLabourLines.description: Staging/CI environment hosting (cloud infra) for ~3 months
Stripe integration sandbox & webhook testing tooling
Legacy data migration tooling / ETL licence (Oracle export tooling)
Data migration validation & dry-run environment (temp DB instance)
Contingency reserve for schedule/scope risk (~7% of labour)

assumptions: No historical actuals (real spend data) are available for this project; estimate is based purely on story-point sizing and role-mix judgement, so uncertainty is wider than usual.
1 story point ≈ 6-7 hours of blended engineering effort, adjusted per task by role mix (backend/frontend/QA/DevOps split based on task nature).
Delivery window assumed at ~13 weeks (3 months), used only to sanity-check that allocated hours fit within each role's FTE capacity (37.5 hrs/week/FTE).

Backend Developer (565 hrs) and DevOps Engineer (115 hrs) are running close to full capacity relative to their FTE (1.5 and 0.4 respectively) over the assumed window; DevOps in particular is thinly staffed for the CI/staging setup (PW-1) and migration cutover (PW-8) — a scheduling risk.
QA Engineer at 0.6 FTE (198 hrs allocated) is adequate but leaves little slack for regression cycles if scope grows, especially around payments (PW-7) and migration validation (PW-8).
Legacy data migration (PW-8) is treated as backend + DevOps + QA heavy with no frontend work; its scale (400k records, 2M invoice lines) carries the highest estimation uncertainty in the backlog.
Payment provider integration (PW-7) assumes Stripe (not a bespoke gateway) and includes webhook + reconciliation logic; costs would rise materially if PCI scope or multi-provider support is required.
Non-labour costs are modest, reflecting a cloud-hosted, mostly-managed-services stack (no on-prem hardware).
Priority-based cost breakdown is derived proportionally from story points times blended cost-per-point, not from independently costing each task by priority.
Contingency of ~7% of labour cost is included as a non-labour reserve line to cover general estimation risk, separate from the pessimistic scenario.

reductions.description: Defer Legacy Data Migration (PW-8) to a phase 2 after portal launch, migrating only active/recent customer records initially instead of the full 400k/2M dataset.
reductions.effect: Removes ~80% of PW-8 backend/DevOps/QA hours from this phase; portal can launch with a subset of data and backfill later.

reductions.description: Descope custom Design System (PW-2) in favor of an existing Angular Material / third-party component library with light theming instead of building tables/dialogs/tokens from scratch.
reductions.effect: Cuts most of the 70 Frontend + 15 QA hours allocated to PW-2 down to light integration and theming work only.

reductions.description: Reduce QA hours on Medium-priority items (PW-2, PW-6) by relying on developer-led testing and automated regression suites instead of dedicated QA passes.
reductions.effect: Removes ~30 QA hours from PW-2 and PW-6 combined; slightly raises defect risk on lower-priority features.

reductions.description: Postpone non-critical CI/staging enhancements (e.g. advanced deployment slots) in PW-1 to a minimal single-environment pipeline for MVP.
reductions.effect: Cuts ~25 DevOps hours and reduces staging environment hosting cost line.

reductions.description: Trim contingency reserve from 7% to 4% of labour once CI pipeline (PW-1) proves estimation accuracy on early sprints.
reductions.effect: Reduces non-labour contingency line; only advisable after first sprint retrospective confirms estimates are tracking well.
